@@133965701 <p> " Vigil , " the brilliant and confounding new novel from Booker Prize winner George Saunders , begins with the narrator falling from the sky : " What a lovely home I found myself plummeting toward , acquiring , as I fell , arms , hands , legs , feet , all of which , as usual , became more substantial with each passing second . " <p> Our narrator plunges headfirst into the driveway . " My rear was in the air , my fresh new legs bicycling energetically . " <p> Recovering herself , she passes through the front door of the house in search of her " charge , " finding him upstairs in the guest room , close to death , " a tiny , crimped fellow in an immense mahogany bed . " <p> ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW <p> " At such moments , " she muses , " I especially cherished my task . I could comfort . I could . " <p> It is a moment of fundamental human connection , and one that is essential to remember as " Vigil " continues @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Random House , 192 pages , $37.99 . <p> As readers , we find ourselves , just a few pages into a relatively short book , facing one of the greatest of mysteries -- our death and what lies beyond -- wrapped within a series of questions : who is the dying man , and , perhaps more pressingly , who , and what , is our narrator ? <p> Some of the answers come quickly . The dying man is K.J. Boone , a **28;28;TOOLONG oil magnate and a key player in climate change denial , lingering in his final hours as a wedding takes place in the yard next door and he is visited by figures from his past and by those whose lives and worlds he has destroyed . <p> Our narrator is Jill " Doll " Blaine , who was a 22-year-old , blissfully happy newlywed , a telephone operator and occasional waitress , when she was " elevated " in 1976 when a bomb destroyed her car . Her role is to bring comfort to the dying , a task she has performed hundreds of @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ had given me . " <p> The set-up is familiar : a little bit " Citizen Kane , " a soupcon of Dickens ' " A Christmas Carol " in contemporary dress . And if that were all there were to " Vigil , " most readers would be grudgingly satisfied : the novel works at that level , albeit somewhat clumsily , a little too earnestly , almost sentimental in places . <p> ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW <p> ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW <p> But Saunders has never been so simple a writer , so obvious . <p> Consider Jill Blaine . We learn her identity in piecemeal fashion as she puts it together herself , slowly arranging fragments -- objects , people , images , isolated by quotation marks -- into a context that eventually forms a sense of her past life : <p> I myself , I recalled , had , in that previous realm , driven several " autos , " the first of which had been " Chevelle . " " Chevelle , " packed with " girlfriends , " as well as my cousin , " Steve @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ " movie-film " unscrolling upon a distant wall of white , surrounded by other autos , all of us learning from the movie-film such things as : Rome is romantic and interesting . <p> It 's a similar process to the " acquiring " of physical form as she falls in the opening paragraph . <p> This gradual accrual of identity complicates the question of Jill 's nature . She dismisses the idea of being a ghost when Boone suggests the possibility , referring to herself as " a friend ... Of sorts ... Here to comfort you . In your hour of need . " Nor does she fit the characteristics of an angel , although she refers to " our great God in Heaven . " Angels , after all , generally do n't fall ( save Lucifer and his followers ) . Nor are they , theologically speaking , former human beings who have forgotten their pasts . <p> Despite being one of the more difficult-to-pigeonhole writers currently at work , Saunders has been stereotyped multiple times over the course of his career . As a prizewinning @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ absurdist , a satirist , a writer 's writer . Following his 2013 convocation speech at Syracuse University , which went viral and was subsequently published in book form as " Congratulations , By the Way , " he became " the ultimate teacher of kindness and of craft , " as the National Book Foundation called him . Following the 2017 publication of his first novel , " Lincoln in the Bardo , " for which Saunders was awarded the Booker Prize , he became viewed as both a literary and spiritual guru , his Buddhist beliefs integrating with his writing talent . <p> With " Vigil , " Saunders seems to be drawing upon and interrogating each of those aspects of himself and his work , to complex and dazzling effect . <p> With the slapstick antics of Jill and her " ilk " and the broad swipes against both climate change deniers and performative " libdopes , " we are in the harder-edged , surreally comic world of early Saunders . Jill , with her relentless focus on " comfort , " probably would have carried a @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ her purse , had she lived a few more decades . In her nature , and her actions , " elevated " Jill hearkens back to the Bodhisattva , an enlightened being in Buddhism who eschews Nirvana in favour of remaining in the cycle of rebirth to help others reach enlightenment . <p> ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW <p> ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW <p> And if a synthesis of and reckoning with Saunders ' life and world views are all there was to " Virgil , " even more readers would be satisfied . <p> But that 's still not all there is to it . <p> The novel 's closing pages have one final turn -- not so much a twist as a delayed understanding -- which triggers a reframing of the book as a whole . Because yes , this is a somewhat clumsy " Christmas Carol " pastiche . And it is also a rich consolidation of Saunders ' oeuvre . <p> But it is also , at its core , a reminder of both the potential and the seeming impossibility of our shared humanity . Jill , for example @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ while Boone sees her a ghost because that 's how she fits into his world view . Saunders acknowledges his own culpability . His ( unlabelled ) depiction of her as a Bodhisattva is no more privileged than any other perspective ; it 's simply how she fits into his thinking . Our world is fractured by our disparate perspectives upon it . <p> So , what is Jill ? <p> I do n't know . And I suspect Saunders does n't know either . <p> But we recognize " her " presence when we experience it , and we note it in its absence . Consider how we first read of Boone : " tiny " and " crimped , " lost in a huge bed . We immediately recognize his humanity , empathize with his fragility . But that intuitive connection disappears when we learn of who he is , of what he has , unrepentantly , done . <p> " Vigil " is a simply drawn , deeply complex fable of the delicate interconnection of life , human and otherwise , and the current myopia around and @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ about kindness or comfort ; it 's a desperate , beautiful cri de coeur , essential reading as the fractured world teeters above the void .

Plants in wetlands absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere , and much of that carbon becomes locked in wetland soils , rather than being released back into the air , " said Pat Kehoe , acting CEO of DUC , in a statement emailed to The Weather Network . <p> Content continues below <h> Canada wetlands facing numerous stressors <p> Kehoe noted that agriculture , urban expansion and other land uses , particularly in southern , populated regions , have put stress on the remaining wetlands . <p> " Rising temperatures and shifting precipitation patterns also alter the ecological balance , making it harder for many wetland species to survive and reproduce . @@133993424 <h> Share this article <p> Stretching across Canada 's vast boreal region , Boreal Peatlands are wetlands that have been quietly shaping life for thousands of years . <p> Take action for Canada 's boreal region . <p> A beaver at work in the boreal . ( CNW Group/Ducks Unlimited Canada ) <p> An astonishing volume of water is naturally filtered in the boreal . ( CNW Group/Ducks Unlimited Canada ) <p> Overview scene of the boreal . ( CNW Group/Ducks Unlimited Canada ) <p> Canada 's boreal region is one of the most important natural landscapes on Earth . Spanning nearly 1.3 billion acres --about one-third of Canada 's landmass--the boreal forest and its wetlands form one of the planet 's largest intact ecosystems . When undisturbed , the boreal 's peatlands play a vital role mitigating floods , drought , and wildfire . It is estimated that one square metre of peatland in Canada 's boreal region stores about five times more carbon than one square metre of tropical Amazon rainforest . <p> Each spring , the boreal region becomes one of the most important nurseries on the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ shorebirds to waterfowl , return to the boreal to nest and raise their young . For many species , especially ducks , the wetlands of the boreal forest are essential breeding habitat . The health of the boreal directly influences wildlife populations across the entire continent . <p> Unfortunately , less than 15% of the region is under some form of conservation protection . These landscapes store enormous amounts of carbon and play a critical role in mitigating climate change . When wetlands are drained or degraded , those benefits are lost -- and carbon is released back into the atmosphere . Watch Peatlands at Work to learn more . <p> Ducks Unlimited Canada ( DUC ) works with landowners , Indigenous communities , governments , industry and conservation-minded partners across Canada to conserve and restore wetlands and associated habitats . DUC has been active in Canada 's boreal for since 2000 and has set an ambitious goal of putting 300 million acres under conservation by 2030 under the " Boreal For Life " campaign . " <p> Ducks Unlimited Canada ( DUC ) is the country 's largest land conservancy and a leader in wetland conservation . " <p> The pilot study tested four different AI models to see which was best at understanding the nuances of biological language . @@134066078 <p> Scientists at the University of California , Irvine have discovered that climate change is causing nitrous oxide , a potent greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance , to break down in the atmosphere more quickly than previously thought , introducing significant uncertainty into climate projections for the rest of the 21st century . <p> Using extended satellite observations from NASA 's Microwave Limb Sounder spanning two decades ( 2004-2024 ) , researchers from UC Irvine 's Department of Earth System Science found that N2O 's atmospheric lifetime is decreasing at a rate of 1.4 percent per decade . With atmospheric concentrations reaching approximately 337 parts per billion in 2024 and increasing at about 3 percent per decade , understanding N2O 's behavior is critical for both climate change mitigation and stratospheric ozone protection efforts , according to Prather . <p> The research reveals that projecting atmospheric N2O abundance involves not just understanding emissions from agriculture , industry and natural sources , but also accounting for how climate change affects the stratospheric sink where N2O is destroyed . The stratosphere is the atmospheric layer about 10 to 50 kilometers above Earth 's surface . <p> Key findings outlined in the PNAS paper include the revelation that the current mean lifetime of N2O is 117 years , but that is decreasing at approximately a year and a half per decade . @@134102980 <p> Rosie DiManno is a Toronto-based columnist covering sports and current affairs for the Star . Follow her on Twitter : @rdimanno . <p> MILAN This city must still be in her hair rollers and slip . <p> Surely , before the guests formally arrive for Friday 's opening ceremony of the XXV Winter Olympics , she 'll be all set to fling open the front door and announce : Avanti ! Avanti ! <p> But as the hours tick down to the curtain going up , Milan is swathed in rain , mist and fog -- Venice is the only Italian city that is at its most beguiling swathed in rain , mist and fog -- hunched in on itself , collar turned up , with scarcely any Games vibe in the air beyond a series of illuminated sports images hanging above the cobblestone streets that lead into Piazza del Duomo , site of the Olympic megastore ( which is rather sacrilegious , cheek by jowl with the masterpiece cathedral ) , projections onto historic buildings , some Olympic-themed billboards shilling major Games sponsors , and the Olympic cauldron @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Though few seemed to take much notice of these barebone adornments this week . Perhaps this is just Milano being Milano , reflexively haughty and disdainful in its aggressively chic presentation , a city that wears understatedly elegant Armani ( favourite native son ) on its sleeves . An Ipsos poll released on Friday showed that 17 per cent of Italians were unaware that the Games were imminent and eight per cent did n't know Italy was hosting the Olympics at all . <p> ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW <p> Of course , the aura of disinterest could simply be due to these Games being so widely spread out -- and spread thin , in clusters -- split-hosted by Milan for ice sports and Cortina d'Ampezzo in the mountain region for snow sports , some 400 kilometres away . Which , sadly , appears to be the sprawling and chopped-up fate of future Winter Games , starting with the generic " French Alps " hosting in 2030 . <p> Climate change is the primary culprit , rapidly shrinking the number of reliable hosts for the winter version of the quadrennial spectacle . @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ from the University of Waterloo , suggests that only about half of a possible 93 locations could reliably host the Winter Games , at least in February , by mid-century , if global warning continues its upwards trajectory . That research indicates snow-making would become a critical issue not far down the road -- and has been already , since at least Vancouver in 2010 . As I recall , Nagano in 1998 was a sloshy mess too . <p> Making the snow , rather than counting on what falls from the sky , has been used to some extent at every Winter Games since Lake Placid in 1980 , but Beijing was the first to rely on it almost entirely in 2022 . Without the manufactured version , the aforementioned research submits that only seven cities could reliably host the Games right now . <p> For these Games , organizers planned to make about 2.4 million cubic metres of snow . No such problem existed when Cortina d'Ampezzo hosted the Games seven decades ago , although some snow was trucked in by the military from the Dolomites . According @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ have climbed by more than three degrees Celsius since they last hosted the Winter Games in 1956 and the area now experiences 41 fewer days of temperatures below freezing than it did in the ' 40s . At the Turin Games in 2006 , organizers faced a crisis of snow au naturel as well , forcing a heavy last-minute reliance on the artificial stuff . <p> Perhaps it 's a winter wonderland up in Cortina . Ca n't really tell from my Milan location , though I 'm watching alpine skiing training on closed-circuit TV at the moment and a lot of the skiers are wiping out . This too -- unsafe competitive conditions for athletes -- is cited as a consequence of insufficient snow depths . Legendary Lindsey Vonn , attempting a comeback at age 41 , ruptured her ACL in a training crash last week but is adamant she 'll still compete . <p> Milan-Cortina was attractive to the International Olympic Committee because it would see a return to a historical cradle of alpine sports in Europe , following Games in China and South Korea . Making use @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ hallmark backdrops , in the summer of ' 24 -- was a further plus , with only the athletes village and main hockey arena built for the purpose . <p> But as of Wednesday , and the first women 's hockey games , the far-flung Santagiulia arena was still a construction site amidst panicky last-minute completion work ( all of the " Milan " venues are actually far outside the city , another reason for the lack of Olympics buzz ) , the new cable-car system intended to carry spectators to the women 's alpine skiing competition will definitely not be finished in time , and frantic work likewise continues at the overhauled old Eugenio Monti sliding track . To say nothing of the track 's 118-million-euro price tag -- a huge cost overrun , after organizers firmly rejected IOC urging that the events be moved to Austria or Switzerland . <p> A dual-country hosting arrangement could not be swallowed . But these were supposed to be Games of a reasonable cost , estimated at 5.2 billion euros . <p> Capacity to host and catastrophic costs have weeded out cities @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ beyond a return to Salt Lake City in 2034 . Frankly , the Winter Games are n't sustainable as devised . They 're fuelling their own demise . @@134103056 <h> For firefighters , dual health crises smoulder <p> Canadian firefighters must have the support they need to be healthy enough to do their jobs . In order to keep saving the rest of us , firefighters need to be able to save themselves.Darren Calabrese/The Canadian Press <p> Firefighters have a romanticized image as stalwart saviours , the buff picture of health fit for a pin-up calendar . Behind the gloss , though , the profession suffers from the dual crises of mental health issues and cancer that kills more of them than fire does . <p> This is not to say that firefighters are n't saviours . They are , coming to the rescue of Canadians daily and facing increasingly complex risks as forest fires threaten cities . But the job takes a serious toll that can not be ignored . <p> By a number of metrics , firefighting is a particularly dangerous career . Firefighters have higher rates of fatal cancer than the general population . They also think about suicide and die by their own hand more than other Canadians . Workplace insurance claims reveal soaring mental @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ made harder by the risks of the job . Addressing firefighter health is not only good for them -- the primary objective -- it 's good for everyone else . <p> Canadians have spent decades building homes that sprawl into the countryside . At the same time , climate change is bringing warmer and drier weather , which will make forest fires larger and more intense . The country needs more firefighting capacity , not less . <p> January was firefighter cancer awareness month and a recent study highlighted the importance of that message . <p> According to a December paper in the journal Injury Epidemiology , Canadian workers ' compensation claim data from 2007 to 2021 showed that cancer accounted for nearly 85 per cent of deaths in the firefighting community , which includes active-duty and retirees . That incidence , nearly 994 deaths per 100,000 firefighters , was more than four times last year 's national average for cancer . <p> Cancer has long been recognized as a risk for firefighters . All smoke is carcinogenic and can be particularly harmful in urban blazes , where burning materials @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ chemicals have also been linked with cancer . <p> An oncologist named Kenneth Kunz who works with the firefighting community draws a rather poetic parallel between fire and cancer . Both can lurk quietly before growing rapidly . Both have the power to consume , to destroy . <p> Like fire , many cancers can also be managed , if caught early , with less invasive efforts and less destruction . <p> Statistics Canada , in partnership with Health Canada and the firefighting industry , is currently working to establish a cancer registry . The goals include facilitating large-scale studies of cancer incidence and assessing the effectiveness of interventions . This seems overdue . <p> Funding for firehouse decontamination equipment could help crews clean smoke-related toxins off their gear . Team leaders can encourage cancer screening as part of training , the same as keeping up physical fitness . <p> When firefighters do get cancer , they face a patchwork of workplace insurer approaches . Only some cancers are accepted as presumptively related to the job , under some circumstances , in some jurisdictions . Better to err on the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Firefighters step up for Canadians . The country must be there for them . <p> First responders have traditionally worked in a suck-it-up culture . But there are promising signs that the hazards of firefighting are being taken more seriously . Certainly , many more of them are being diagnosed with mental health concerns , which could reflect a willingness to be open about once-stigmatized conditions . <p> That study in Injury Epidemiology showed that the annual number of claims for firefighter injuries related to mental illness rose by nearly 1,500 per cent between 2007 and 2021 . <p> The researchers do not speculate on the reasons for the rise but note that firefighting is associated with post-traumatic stress disorder , burnout and depression . They also point out that their numbers may not capture the full severity of the situation , since they do n't include rejected claims . <p> A separate effort led by researchers at the University of Regina is looking this month for firefighters to participate in a study of mental health . The results could inform government policy and , hopefully , many will step @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ need to be healthy enough to do their jobs . In order to keep saving the rest of us , firefighters need to be able to save themselves .

Initial drilling results from this discovery , made in a relatively under-explored area of the mine concession , demonstrate that the WZD target is highly prospective for additional discoveries . <p> Given the significance of the WZD target , DPM has planned an additional 10,000 metres of drilling , which is expected to be completed within the first quarter of 2026 . The Company expects the Chelopech North concession in 2026 , which is an area of 4.6 square kilometers surrounding the Chelopech mine concession . @@134103298 <h> Letter of the Day Jamaica can not sing its way to power <p> As Jamaica observes Black History Month and Reggae Month , we rightly celebrate a legacy of resistance , creativity , and cultural achievement that has amplified the nation 's global presence . Reggae taught the world how to speak truth to power , and Black history highlights survival as an act of defiance . Yet celebration alone is not strategy , and cultural accomplishment can not substitute for the structural forms of power required in today 's world . <p> Jamaica , like much of the Caribbean , is being nudged into choosing sides within a polarized global landscape . These choices -- framed as partnerships or development opportunities -- mask a familiar outcome : dependence . Without strengthening scientific and technological capacity , Jamaica 's ability to protect its interests will remain limited regardless of geopolitical alignments . <p> Modern power rests not primarily on ideology or military force but on technology , data , energy systems , and production . Countries lacking indigenous STEM capacity do not remain neutral ; they become dependent , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ expertise . Jamaica 's pride in its cultural influence is justified , but our national narrative rarely elevates engineers , scientists , or inventors with the same enthusiasm as artists and athletes . This imbalance leaves us vulnerable . <p> The tension between culture and STEM is a false one . Reggae itself grew out of technological innovation -- sound engineering , experimentation , and adaptation . The creativity that fuels Jamaican culture can also drive scientific and technical success , but only if the country deliberately nurtures it . Though Jamaican innovators have contributed to agriculture , medicine , and engineering , their stories remain peripheral , and the education system continues training young people primarily as consumers rather than creators of technology . <h> Headlines Delivered to Your Inbox <p> Global challenges -- including climate change , supply chain fragility , digital surveillance , and energy insecurity -- will intensify in coming decades . Small states without technical competence will be forced to react rather than lead , and sovereignty risks becoming ceremonial . Black History Month reminds us that freedom without power is fragile ; Reggae Month @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ includes scientific literacy , technical confidence , and economic self reliance . It demands laboratories as much as lyrics , workshops as much as world stages . <p> If Jamaica is to avoid recurring cycles of dependency , we must expand our understanding of nation-building . Cultural pride must be matched with technical ambition , and symbolic sovereignty reinforced with real capability . Culture has given Jamaica its voice ; science and technology will determine whether that voice carries weight in a rapidly reorganizing world .

@@134139992 <h> MP Kirsty Duncan became a crusader for safety in sport <p> Outspoken , curious and compassionate , Kirsty Duncan believed that when people told her things were " impossible , " they were simply daring her to prove them wrong . <p> As a medical geographer , professor and author , as a federal cabinet minister in charge of science and sport , as a Highland dancer and as a speaker of Gaelic who once won a prize for a poem she wrote in that language , she spent her life taking on dares . Boe may be misleading , particularly if used in isolation . A boe conversion ratio of 6 Mcf:1 bbl is based on an energy equivalency conversion method primarily applicable at the burner tip and does not represent a value equivalency at the wellhead . Given that the value ratio based on the current price of crude oil as compared to natural gas is significantly different than the energy equivalency of the 6:1 conversion ratio , utilizing the 6:1 conversion ratio may be misleading as an indication of value . <p> Represents average daily production divided by the diluted weighted average common shares outstanding for the three months ended December 31 . <p> ( 4 ) <p> This is a specified financial measure . Consistent with previous years , the strategy is underpinned by its longstanding principles of safety , capital discipline , and preserving a strong balance sheet . <p> Operations Update <p> Attachie <p> At over 360 net sections , Attachie is a large condensate-rich asset and remains in the early stages of development . In 2025 , its first year of operations , ARC focused on capturing and applying learnings to deliver repeatable well performance and improved capital efficiencies to ensure long-term profitability at the asset . <p> The early production results from the most recent Upper Montney pads at Attachie , brought on stream in late 2025 and early 2026 , have been variable and below expectations . In response , ARC has adjusted its development schedule to further evaluate well performance and determine an appropriate development plan for Attachie going forward . As a result , ARC is removing asset-level production guidance at Attachie for 2026 . <p> ARC remains confident in the long-term potential of the resource at Attachie . The Company will continue to advance the asset in a disciplined manner , allocating capital to further refine well design and apply operational learnings . <p> 2026 Guidance <p> Corporate guidance for 2026 remains unchanged . Asset-level production contribution and capital allocation may shift throughout the year as the development plan for Attachie evolves . <p> Average annual production of between 405,000 and 420,000 boe per day ( 61 per cent natural gas and 39 per cent crude oil and liquids ) . <p> Planned capital expenditures of between $1.8 to $1.9 billion(1) . <p> Based on the current forward curve and Company guidance , ARC estimates 2026 free funds flow of approximately $1.2 billion(2) , essentially all of which is earmarked for shareholder returns via the base dividend and share repurchases . <p> ARC 's 2026 corporate guidance is based on various commodity price scenarios and economic conditions . Production guidance does not include any assumption for possible natural gas production curtailments due to low natural gas prices . Certain guidance estimates may fluctuate with commodity price changes and regulatory changes . Production increased seven per cent compared to the fourth quarter of 2024 and 10 per cent on a per share basis . <p> The increase year-over-year was driven primarily by the Kakwa Acquisition . During the fourth quarter , production at Kakwa averaged 215,073 boe per day ( 42 per cent natural gas and 58 per cent crude oil and liquids ) , which included 124,505 barrels per day of condensate and natural gas liquids . <p> Attachie production averaged 28,286 boe per day during the fourth quarter ( 41 per cent natural gas and 59 per cent crude oil and liquids ) , and included 13,182 barrels per day of condensate . <p> Natural gas production at Sunrise was restored in the fourth quarter when AECO natural gas prices recovered . <p> Full-Year 2025 <p> Full-year production averaged 374,336 boe per day ( 59 per cent natural gas and 41 per cent crude oil and liquids ) , which was in line with Company guidance . <p> This included record average crude oil and condensate production of 106,984 barrels per day , driven primarily by Attachie and the Kakwa Acquisition that closed on July 2 , 2025 . <p> The natural gas production curtailments at Sunrise that occurred from July through October reduced full-year average production by approximately 12,000 boe per day . This allowed ARC to defer approximately $50 million of capital expenditures earmarked to sustain production at Sunrise . <p> ARC generated $874 million ( $1.52 per share ) of funds from operations in the fourth quarter . This represents a 13 per cent increase ( $104 million or $0.22 per share ) compared to the same quarter of the prior year , driven primarily by higher production at Kakwa and Attachie . <p> ARC reported free funds flow of $415 million ( $0.72 per share ) in the fourth quarter . <p> Full-Year 2025 <p> In 2025 , ARC generated funds from operations of $3.2 billion ( $5.48 per share ) and cash In 2025 , ARC distributed 75 per cent of free funds flow or $966 million ( $1.66 per share ) to shareholders through a combination of dividends and share repurchases under its NCIB . The remainder was allocated to debt reduction to preserve ARC 's financial strength . <p> In the third quarter of 2025 , the Board approved an increase of 11 per cent to the Company 's quarterly dividend , from $0.19 per share to $0.21 per share ( $0.76 per share to $0.84 per share , per annum ) . <p> During the fourth quarter , ARC declared dividends of $120 million ( $0.21 per share ) and repurchased 5.1 million common shares under its NCIB at a weighted average price of $26.86 per share . <p> In 2025 , ARC repurchased 19.7 million common shares under its NCIB at a weighted average price of $26.09 per share throughout the year . <p> Since commencing its initial NCIB in September 2021 , ARC has repurchased approximately 22 per cent ( 159 million common shares ) of its total outstanding shares at a weighted average price of $17.74 per share . <p> ARC intends to distribute essentially all free funds flow to shareholders in 2026 through its growing base dividend and continued share repurchases . <p> Operating , Transportation , and General and Administrative Expense <p> Operating Expense <p> ARC 's fourth quarter 2025 operating expense of $5.18 per boe was 19 per cent or $1.18 per boe lower than the previous quarter . The decrease in operating costs per boe is primarily due to Sunrise volumes being restored and the completion of planned maintenance activity . <p> Full-year 2025 operating expense of $5.39 per boe was in line with Company guidance . <p> Transportation Expense <p> ARC 's fourth quarter 2025 transportation expense per boe of $4.83 decreased by four per cent or $0.20 per boe compared to the same period in the prior year . <p> ARC 's full-year 2025 transportation expense of $5.04 per boe was at the low end of ARC 's guidance range of $5.00 to $5.50 per boe . <p> General and Administrative Expense <p> ARC 's fourth quarter 2025 general and administrative expense per boe of $1.26 decreased 33 per cent from the same period of the prior year , primarily due to the revaluation of the liability associated with ARC 's share-based compensation plans . <p> ARC 's full-year 2025 general and administrative expense of $1.28 per boe decreased 34 per cent compared to the prior year and was slightly lower than the Company guidance range of $1.30 to $1.50 per boe . <p> Cash Flow Used in Investing Activities and Capital Expenditures <p> Cash flow used in investing activities was $476 million during the fourth quarter of 2025 . ARC invested $459 million in capital expenditures to drill 39 wells and complete 32 wells . The increase in net income compared to the prior year was primarily due to an increase in production volumes partially offset by an increase in unrealized losses on risk management contracts . <p> 2025 RESERVES <p> Highlights <p> ARC reported record reserves in 2025 across all categories , including PDP , 1P , and 2P . PDP and 2P reserves increased by 15 per cent and nine per cent , respectively , compared to 2024 . <p> ARC 's before-tax NPV for 2P reserves of $22.1 billion ( discounted at 10 per cent ) equates to $38.71 per share . ARC 's 2P NPV includes the development of 23 per cent of ARC 's internal estimate of drilling inventory . <p> ARC 's before-tax PDP NPV of $17.54 per share , discounted at 10 per cent , increased six per cent year-over-year . <p> ARC 's NPV was determined using 3CA forecast pricing and foreign exchange rates at January 1 , 2026 , with a 10-year average WTI price of US$73.01 per barrel and a 10-year average AECO price of $3.64 per MMBtu . <p> In 2025 , ARC replaced 121 per cent of its 2P reserves . For the 18th consecutive year , 2P reserve replacement from development has been 120 per cent of produced reserves or greater . <p> 2P reserves of 2,277 MMboe were a Company record , driven by the Kakwa Acquisition and organic reserve growth . <p> ARC booked an additional 151 MMboe of 2P reserves as a result of the Kakwa Acquisition . <p> PDP finding , development and acquisition ( " FD&amp;A " ) costs , including future development capital ( " FDC " ) of $15.77 per boe(1) equated to a 1.6 times(1) PDP FD&amp;A recycle ratio . <p> FDC for 2P reserves totalled $11.3 billion at December 31 , 2025 compared to $10.3 billion at December 31 , 2024 . under ARC 's SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca . <p> NON-GAAP AND OTHER FINANCIAL MEASURES <p> Throughout this news release and in other materials disclosed by the Company , ARC employs certain measures to analyze its financial performance , financial position , and cash flow . These non-GAAP and other financial measures are not standardized financial measures under IFRS Accounting Standards and may not be comparable to similar financial measures disclosed by other issuers . The non-GAAP and other financial measures should not be considered to be more meaningful than generally accepted accounting principles ( " GAAP " ) measures which are determined in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards , such as net income , cash flow from operating activities , and cash flow used in investing activities , as indicators of ARC 's performance . <p> Non-GAAP Financial Measures <p> Capital Expenditures <p> ARC uses capital expenditures to monitor its capital investments relative to those budgeted by the Company on an annual basis . ARC 's capital budget excludes acquisition or disposition activities as well as the accounting impact of any accrual changes and payments under certain lease arrangements . The most directly comparable GAAP measure to capital expenditures is cash flow used in investing activities . The following table details the composition of capital expenditures and its reconciliation to cash flow used in investing activities . <p> Capital Expenditures <p> ( $ millions ) <p> Three Months Ended <p> Year Ended <p> September 30 , 2025 <p> December 31 , 2025 <p> December 31 , 2024 <p> December 31 , 2025 <p> December 31 , 2024 <p> Cash flow used in investing activities <p> 2,160.0 <p> 475.5 <p> 423.3 <p> 3,536.0 <p> 1,906.2 <p> Business combination <p> ( 1,672.1 ) <p> -- <p> -- <p> ( 1,672.1 ) <p> 0 <p> Acquisition of assets <p> ( 10.6 ) <p> ( 2.4 ) <p> ( 8.8 ) <p> ( 17.8 ) <p> ( 13.9 ) <p> Disposal of assets <p> -- <p> -- <p> -- <p> 4.0 <p> 80.0 <p> Long-term investments <p> ( 0.8 ) <p> ( 1.5 ) <p> ( 2.1 ) <p> ( 3.5 ) <p> ( 6.8 ) <p> Change in non-cash investing working capital <p> 9.6 <p> ( 21.8 ) <p> ( 70.9 ) <p> 26.1 <p> ( 146.5 ) <p> Capitalized right-of-use asset depreciation <p> 10.3 <p> 9.1 <p> 8.5 <p> 36.0 <p> 26.5 <p> Capital expenditures <p> 496.4 <p> 458.9 <p> 350.0 <p> 1,908.7 <p> 1,845.5 <p> Free Funds Flow <p> ARC uses free funds flow as an indicator of the efficiency and liquidity of ARC 's business , measuring its funds after capital investment available to manage debt levels , and return capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases . ARC computes free funds flow as funds from operations generated during the period less capital expenditures . Capital expenditures is a non-GAAP financial measure . By removing the impact of current period capital expenditures from funds from operations , Management monitors its free funds flow to inform its capital allocation decisions . The most directly comparable GAAP measure to free funds flow is cash flow from operating activities . Adjusted net capital acquisitions is useful as it provides a measure of cash , debt , and share consideration used to acquire crude oil and natural gas assets during the period , net of cash provided by the disposal of any crude oil and natural gas assets during the period . Free funds flow is a non-GAAP financial measure . Management believes that free funds flow per share provides investors an indicator of funds generated from the business that could be allocated to each shareholder 's equity position . <p> Finding and Development Costs <p> ARC calculates F&amp;D costs as capital expenditures divided by the change in reserves within the applicable reserves category . ARC calculates F&amp;D costs , including FDC , as the sum of capital expenditures and the change in FDC required to bring the reserves on production , divided by the change in reserves within the applicable reserves category . Capital expenditures , a non-GAAP financial measure , is used as a component of F&amp;D costs . Management uses F&amp;D costs as a measure of capital efficiency for organic reserves development . <p> Finding , Development and Acquisition Costs <p> ARC calculates FD&amp;A costs as the sum of capital expenditures and adjusted net capital acquisitions divided by the change in reserves within the applicable reserves category , inclusive of changes due to acquisitions and dispositions . ARC calculates FD&amp;A costs , including FDC , as the sum of capital expenditures , adjusted net capital acquisitions , and the change in FDC required to bring the reserves on production , divided by the change in reserves within the applicable reserves category , inclusive of changes due to acquisitions and dispositions . Capital expenditures and adjusted net capital acquisitions , both non-GAAP financial measures , are used as components of FD&amp;A costs . Management uses FD&amp;A costs as a measure of capital efficiency for organic and acquired reserves development . <p> Recycle Ratio <p> ARC calculates recycle ratio by dividing the netback per boe by F&amp;D or FD&amp;A costs . Netback per boe is a non-GAAP ratio that uses netback , a non-GAAP financial measure , as a component . Capital expenditures , a non-GAAP financial measure , is used as a component of F&amp;D costs . Capital expenditures and adjusted net capital acquisitions , both non-GAAP financial measures , are used as components of FD&amp;A costs . Management uses recycle ratio to relate the cost of adding reserves to the expected cash flows to be generated . <p> Supplementary Financial Measures <p> Before-tax Proved plus Probable Net Present Value per Share <p> Before-tax 2P NPV per share is comprised of the before-tax NPV for 2P reserves , discounted at 10 per cent , as determined in accordance with NI 51-101 , divided by divided by common shares outstanding at the end of the period . <p> Capital Management Measures <p> Funds from operations , net debt , and net debt to funds from operations are capital management measures . Reserves are classified according to the degree of certainty associated with the estimates as follows : <p> Proved Reserves are those reserves that can be estimated with a high degree of certainty to be recoverable . It is likely that the actual remaining quantities recovered will exceed the estimated proved reserves . <p> Probable Reserves are those additional reserves that are less certain to be recovered than proved reserves . It is equally likely that the actual remaining quantities recovered will be greater or less than the sum of the estimated proved plus probable reserves . <p> In accordance with Canadian practice , production volumes and revenues are reported on a company gross basis , before deduction of Crown and other royalties , and without including any royalty interests , unless otherwise stated . Unless otherwise specified , all reserves volumes in this news release ( and all information derived therefrom ) are based on company gross reserves using forecast prices and costs . <p> This news release contains metrics commonly used in the crude oil and natural gas industry . These metrics do not have standardized meanings and may not be comparable to similar metrics disclosed by other issuers . See " Non-GAAP and Other Financial Measures " of this news release and the definitions of reserve replacement , reserves life index and finding and development costs below . Management uses these metrics for its own performance measurements and to provide shareholders with measures to compare ARC 's performance over time ; however , such measures are not reliable indicators of ARC 's future performance and future performance may not compare to the performance in previous periods : <p> Reserves replacement is calculated by dividing the annual reserves additions , in boe , by ARC 's annual production , in boe . Management uses this measure to determine the relative change of its reserves base over a period of time . <p> Reserves life index ( " RLI " ) is calculated by dividing the reserves by the average annual production for that period . Management uses this measure to determine the relative change of its reserves base over a period of time . PDP RLI is calculated by dividing the proved developed producing reserves by the average annual production for that period . 2P RLI is calculated by dividing the proved plus probable reserves by the average annual production for that period . Management uses this measure to determine the relative change of its reserves base over a period of time . <p> Finding and development costs are calculated as capital expenditures divided by the change in reserves within the applicable reserves category . See " Non-GAAP and Other Financial Measures " for additional information about this metric . <p> This news release contains estimates of the NPV of the Company 's future net revenue from reserves associated with ARC 's assets . Such amounts do not represent the fair market value of such reserves . The recovery and reserve estimates provided herein are estimates only and there is no guarantee that the estimated reserves will be recovered . The NPV of the assets ' base production is a snapshot in time and is based on the reserves evaluated using applicable pricing assumptions . It should not be assumed that the undiscounted or discounted NPV of future net revenue attributable to the assets represents the fair market value of those assets . The estimates for reserves for individual properties may not reflect the same confidence level as estimates of reserves for all properties due to the effects of aggregation . The recovery and reserve estimates of crude oil , natural gas liquids and natural gas reserves are estimates only and there is no guarantee that the estimated reserves will be recovered . @@134140447 <h> Red Deer area reaches record high temperature for February 5 <p> Some record-setting temperatures made their way through central Alberta Thursday , with Red Deer reaching a new record high for February 5 . <p> According to Environment and Climate Change Canada ( ECCC ) , the daytime high in Red Deer on Thursday was 9.0 degrees Celsius , edging out the previous record high for February 5 of 8.9 degrees Celsius set in 1924 . Records in this area have been kept since 1904 . <p> Elsewhere , the Rocky Mountain House area reached 13.8 degrees Celsius on Thursday , surpassing the old record for February 5 of 11.7 set in 1963 . Records in this area have been kept since 1915 . <p> The Sundre area , meantime , hit 13.1 degrees Celsius on Thursday , beating the old record of 11.3 set in 1996 . Records in this area have been kept since 1993 . <p> The Nordegg area reached 15.8 degrees , beating the old record of 11.7 degrees Celsius set in 1954 . Records in this area have been kept since 1915. 
@@134161300 <h> From climate change to Inuit culture -- five things shared by Greenland and Canada <p> NUUK -- Canada is set to formally open its newest diplomatic mission Friday in Nuuk , the capital of Greenland , to build on deep ties that precede the recent geopolitical crisis . <p> U.S. President Donald Trump has demanded U.S. control of Greenland and only recently backed down after the White House refused to rule out securing the island through military force . His demands echoed his repeated calls for Canada to become an American state . <p> In February 2024 , before Trump returned to the White House , the Danish territory launched an Arctic strategy which promised a representation office for Greenland in Ottawa . <p> That December , Canada promised to open a consulate in Nuuk . The building is now operational after a formal launch nearly three months ago was cancelled due to bad weather . <p> Since then , Trump 's aspirations for the territory have drawn global media to Nuuk . <p> Here are five things Canada and Greenland share : <h> A land border <p> In @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ an amicable dispute over Hans Island involving 1.3 square kilometres that both countries had claimed for five decades . <p> The uninhabited rock sits between Ellesmere Island in Nunavut and Greenland . It was divided along a natural ridge , giving about 40 per cent of the territory to Canada and the rest to Greenland . <p> That meant that Canada for the first time shared a land border with Denmark . <p> During the long dispute -- in what was dubbed the Whisky Wars -- soldiers from both nations left bottles of spirits on the island with little notes for one another while removing each other 's flags . <p> The negotiations took 17 years and resolved a disagreement between the two countries over maritime boundaries on the continental shelf . As a way of affirming support for international law , both countries had agreed to refer the dispute to the International Court of Justice if they could n't reach a deal . <p> The agreement followed consultation with Inuit from both Nunavut and Greenland , who maintained hunting rights and freedom of movement on the island . <h> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ in 2022 , Ottawa said the process had prompted further negotiations on freedom of movement for Inuit living in Nunavut and Greenland to make it easier for them to visit friends and family . <p> The territories share many cultural and family ties . <p> The 2021 census reported 70,545 Inuit in Canada , mostly in their ancestral territories in the three territories , Labrador and northern Quebec . <p> Greenland 's population stood at 57,000 and most estimates suggest 90 per cent of the territory is Inuit . <p> Inuit also have worked together across colonial borders to advocate for their rights and the preservation of their cultures through the Inuit Circumpolar Council , which includes representatives from Canada , Greenland , Alaska and Siberia . <p> Greenland suffers from some of the same problems seen across Canada 's North , such as poor health outcomes and a high rate of suicide . But the territory is also part of a Nordic social model that emphasizes medical and educational access . <p> Both Nunavut and Greenland have a measure of autonomy and self-government , but not full sovereignty . @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ caused disproportionate changes in the Far North , affecting the seasons and access to traditional food sources . <p> Canada and Greenland say they want to collaborate more on the fight against climate change through their new diplomatic missions . There 's talk of more research collaboration and integration of scientific and traditional knowledge . <p> The changing climate also increases shipping access around Greenland and Nunavut -- and brings with it heightened fears about adversary nations sending military and research vessels . <p> The Danish armed forces ' leaders in Greenland have talked about improving co-ordination with Canada on northern defence . That effort might be aided by the new defence industry pact Ottawa signed with the European Union last year . <p> Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand has said that after decades of Canadian troops supporting security in Western Europe , it 's time for the NATO military alliance to focus on the North . <h> Mineral wealth <p> Greenland has a wealth of critical minerals that can help fuel the global clean energy transition through the manufacture of solar panels and batteries for electric vehicles . <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ present a strategic vulnerability , western countries have focused on boosting their access to the materials in recent years . <p> Experts have said that extracting minerals from Greenland is particularly complex and expensive due to its location and terrain . <p> An expansion of mining in Greenland might in theory influence Canadian supply chains , which were affected by Canadian sanctions on Russia following its 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine . <p> Some mining equipment had travelled between Canada and Russia before those sanctions took effect . <h> Elbows Up <p> Greenland has seen some very large citizen demonstrations pushing back against talk of annexation by the U.S. <p> Local shops have been selling garments marked " Greenland is not for sale , " similar to the ball caps worn by Ontario Premier Doug Ford that declared " Canada is not for sale . " <p> Online forums and local media show that Greenlanders paid close attention to Trump when he spoke of making Canada a U.S. state . <p> Last August , reports that officials in the Trump administration were actively seeking to promote Greenland 's secession from @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ support making the territory part of the U.S. -- prompted Denmark to summon the U.S. ambassador in Copenhagen . <p> Still , the Trump administration has touched on a widespread desire for independence in the territory , where the political opposition has called for talks with the Americans on a possible sovereignty pact that could be partly bankrolled by American-developed mines . <p> In January , dozens marched in Iqaluit in solidarity with Greenland in response to Trump 's renewed threats to take control of the island . <h> Get the CityNews App <p> Now New and Improved ! @@134171657 <h> Scientists measure sea surface temperatures <p> El Ni ? o occurs when water temperatures around the equator in the eastern Pacific Ocean come in 0.5 ? C warmer than normal for several consecutive months . La Ni ? a is the cold-water opposite of El Ni ? o . <p> These two phenomena are part of a larger pattern known as the El Ni ? o-Southern Oscillation ( ENSO ) , which tracks how the ocean and atmosphere are coupled with one another . <p> One of the major ways scientists keep tabs on ENSO is by tracking ocean temperature anomalies in a key region of the Pacific Ocean known as Ni ? o 3.4 . <p> Sea surface temperatures in this particular section of the ocean are critical to the overall maintenance of El Ni ? o and La Ni ? a conditions . <p> Content continues below <h> A better way to keep tabs on El Ni ? o and La Ni ? a <p> Up until now , scientists have measured ocean temperature anomalies by averaging the temperature across the Ni ? o 3.4 region and @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ resulting temperature anomaly is known as the Oceanic Ni ? o Index ( ONI ) . <p> As climate change causes overall ocean temperatures to increase , comparing current readings to climatology can result in temperatures that seem much warmer than normal , potentially resulting in more frequent El Ni ? o events and less frequent La Ni ? a events . <p> Beginning this February , average ocean temperatures across the Ni ? o 3.4 region will now be compared to average ocean temperatures across the entire global tropics instead of that specific region 's climatology . Think of it like a sliding scale instead of a stationary ruler . <p> Using the old index , the event saw a maximum temperature anomaly of +2.1 ? C. The new index , which takes into account water temperature trends throughout the entire tropics , the maximum anomaly dropped down to just +1.5 ? C instead . <p> Content continues below <p> This switch wo n't just account for the effects of climate change . " This helps to more clearly identify how the ocean and atmosphere interact to reinforce El @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ a varying climate , " the Australian Bureau of Meteorology explained on its website . <p> Ultimately , this change will help forecasters better classify El Ni ? o and La Ni ? a events , improving our understanding and preparation for how these events can affect our seasonal weather patterns here at home .

About which some Canadian athletes are absolutely clueless , judging by their what-the-heck-is-this ? social media postings . <p> NHL pros making north of $12 million this season will be slumming it in Milan , yet thrilled nevertheless for the monk-like cells , after being restored to the Olympics for the first time since 2014 . There are other athletes , too , very nearly as enriched and privileged via huge endorsements deals , who are likewise accustomed to percale sheets and feather-filled pillows and concierge service . But the Olympics are inherently , deliberately , fundamentally egalitarian and classless . Not even a fistful of gold medals will get you a king-sized bed . And some of those Team Canada hockey players are doubling up . <p> " Hockey players can have big backs , " Motokuni Takaoka , chair , president and chief executive officer of airweave , a futon manufacturer , tells me when I wander aimlessly within sales pitch distance of his display corner . " Canadians are very intelligent , " he adds , explaining how the Canadian delegation had ordered 400 futons in advance , to place on top of the provided mattresses , shipped first to Canada and then to Italy . <p> A descriptor of this athletes village that comes to mind is brutalist Russian , as in hulking highrises of sharp angles and bland facades , albeit brightened up at the moment by national flags , a pair of four-storey tall USA banners featuring Stars and Stripes ( an attempt nearby at that annoying USA ! USA ! USA ! chant quickly peters out ) and that here-there-everywhere Team Canada moose . On Thursday , in the Canadian wing , they were holding a name-that-moose contest . I 'm partial to chocolate moose . ) <p> Six moose , in fact , cargo-flown to Milan , one for each of the cluster athletes villages spread out across Lombardy . About half of Canada 's athletes have taken up residence across three floors of the main village . One of them is superstar short-track skater William Dandjinou , expected to bring home a fistful of medals . <p> " It feels like home already . I 've tried to ease myself in . It feels like a Utopian society -- everyone is in shape , everyone has a purpose here . It 's been great meeting other athletes . " <p> They 've done their best to keep the athletes entertained and diverted . Technogym has outfitted a workout hub with all the latest equipment , including a Pilates machine . There 's a mind wellness room for meditation , photo booths , an AI-generated pin trading hub ( a robotic arm picks out a plastic ball , although this strikes me as not so different from those old claw things at drive-in theatres ) , foosball and air hockey tables , a Corona beer octagon with gold laminated bottles onto which athletes can carve their own message , sports-related video games and more techno gizmos than you can shake a stick at , retro board games , Coke cans for embossing your own picture , cafes , and a full cosmetic service . Not to mention that every athlete upon arrival receives a free folding Samsung Galaxy Z , decorated with Olympic laurels . <p> They can also adopt a plant for their room . <p> " I 'm going to be honest , " Dandjinou says . " I 'm not using all of it because it can be quite overwhelming . I 'm here for a reason and I 'm very focused on that reason . I 'm having fun also but there 's so much stuff to do , I know I wo n't be able to do everything . " <p> Maxime Laoun , also a short-track skater , is at his second Games , but of course Beijing four years ago was shrink-wrapped amidst COVID -- no fans in the stands , no families on hand to watch -- so this is a far different experience . <p> " The village is kind of similar , except the buildings were a lot taller in Beijing , " Laoun says . " I was wearing a mask back then and I 'm still wearing masks today . The big difference will be seeing people in the stands . That was the sad part in Beijing . " <p> Athletes , like armies , travel on their stomach . Eating is a key component of everyone 's day and feeding athletes a core responsibility from a platoon of chefs . It is a cornucopia of cuisine in a cavernous dining hall . Thursday 's buffet-style selection : beef , chicken breast , couscous , curried chicken , various pastas , plaice , veal , swordfish , a full deli counter , a wide assortment of cheeses , vegetarian and gluten-free options , focaccia , apple strudel , chocolate cake , and pizza of course . <p> At this village , they serve up to 3,400 meals a day , crack 3,000 eggs , and go through 400 kilograms of meat . <p> When these athletes move out , the paralympic athletes move in . And when the Games are all done and dusted , the village will be turned into the largest student residence in Italy . <h> The Winter Olympics always come with debate . But the reason we watch has never changed <p> The Milan Cortina Olympics will span approximately 8,500 square miles across Northern Italy . <p> Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images Toronto Star <p> MILAN -- Once upon a time the Winter Olympics were Games you could get your arms around . Ice and snow but snug and felicitous . <p> Cortina d'Ampezzo was like that , exactly seven decades ago , after earlier plans were so rudely interrupted by World War II . <p> Now they 're a sprawling behemoth , a compound noun colossus of co-hosts : Milan and Cortina . Spanning approximately 22,000 square kilometres across Northern Italy , some 400 kilometres between the starring cities and just about impossible to get from here to there over tortuous mountain roads . Certainly siloed athletes ca n't do it , should any wish to transition from competitor to gadabout spectator . A ski mountaineering entrant ( the only new sport added for the XXV Games ) , say , who might want to take in a hockey game . <p> These Olympics will go down in history for bringing together the largest number ever of athletes -- 2,900 -- for the winter version spectacle , representing 93 nations -- welcome newcomers Benin and Guinea-Bissau ! ( one alpine skier each ) -- contesting 195 medals in 116 events from 16 disciplines . But scattered among four sports clusters . <p> That was the sustainability thinking from the International Olympic Committee , light on new and permanent construction , heavy on existing venues , all jumbled together under the mantra of environmental prudence and reducing the carbon footprint , even as global warming poses the greatest threat to Games continuity . Allegedly thrifty Games ( as if ) , it was also an inducement to stir up waning interest in potential future hosting countries . Rome , Boston , Hamburg , Barcelona and Budapest are among cities that have recently withdrawn their intention to bid . <p> The cost of hosting is astronomical . The Calgary Games in 1988 came in at a penny-wise $1.2 billion ( all figures U.S. ) ; Vancouver in 2010 had an estimated price tag of $3.2 billion , including $2.1 billion for the Canada Line Sky Train connecting the city to the airport and Richmond . The real cost is still fuzzy , with some pegging the price north of $7 billion . <p> The Olympic rings are pictured on the grounds of the Winter Games in Cortina d'Ampezzo , Italy . <p> Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images Toronto Star <p> Italy went in with eyes wide open , having hosted the Olympics three times before , and leery of creating white elephants . But the country is on the hook for $1.9 billion , the operational budget for Milan Cortina , but again , some have estimated a final bottom line of more than $4 billion . An organization called the Unsustainable Olympics Committee has announced widespread protests for an event " which is already bringing nothing but debt , concrete to cities and mountains , labour exploitation and precarious employment , rising rents , plundering of water resources , and devastation of the highlands . " <p> Well , no , it 's not all grossly that . But is it worth it ? The 2004 Athens Games just about drove Greece into bankruptcy . ( And never have I experienced an Olympic host city more cold-shouldering of the whole extravaganza while the Games were on . ) <p> Milan Cortina may have taken it really easy on the new-build , utilizing 19 pre-existing venues , but the only facility constructed specifically for the Games ( apart from the athletes village ) , the Santagiulia Arena for hockey , remains touch-and-go to be ready on time . Reviews were horrible after a debut test-game in early January , the ice soft and snowy , and a hole opened up in front of one of the nets . <p> Workers walk near the Santagiulia Arena in Milan on Jan. 27 . <p> Marco Bertorello/AFP via Getty Images Toronto Star <p> Yet the hockey tournament , with NHL players returning to the Olympics for the first time since 2014 , is one of the primo showcase events , Canada and the United States at daggers drawn . The U.S. has n't won hockey gold since the Miracle on Ice team at Lake Placid in 1980 . Canada , in an NHL manner of speaking at least , is the defending champion , having copped back-to-back gold in 2010 and 2014 ( Sochi ) . <p> Come what may , all the debate , cynicism and hands wrung , the athletes always rescue the Olympics , no matter how obscure their sport of passion , in the outer reaches far beyond glamorama events such as alpine skiing , hockey and figure skating . If only once every four years , for a fleeting fortnight , TV viewers ( NBC hopes ) are glued even to the likes of luge and biathlon . <p> Sarault leaves Beijing 2022 and medical nightmares behind : " I knew in my soul that it was going to work out for me . " <p> A nation with a population of 5.65 million -- less than the Greater Toronto Area -- has racked up 405 medals , including 148 gold , a legacy mainly built around cross-country skiing , speedskating , biathlon and ski jumping . In Beijing four years ago , they collected a podium-topping 37 medals , 16 of them gold . <p> The U.S. is a distant second , with 330 medals . Canada has punched above its weight , fifth on the overall table with 225 medals . A country that won not a single gold when hosting the Summer Games in Montreal in 1976 is long past just wanting to participate . Own the Podium , launched two decades ago , pumped about $110 million into prioritizing funding for national sports organizations with the objective of achieving heady results in Vancouver . And nailed it -- No. 1 , 26 medals , 14 gold . <p> A team of 207 athletes this time -- the oldest 44-year-old curler Marc Kennedy ; the youngest 18-year-old snowboarder Eli Bouchard -- boasts medal-worth veterans and Olympic rookies : Co-flag-bearer Mika ? l Kingsbury , competing in his fourth Games , with a gold and two silvers in his Olympic trophy chest , is aiming for the podium in moguls and dual moguls ; short-track speedskating sensation William Dandjinou is contesting three individual race distances and at least one relay , while teammate Courtney Sarault ( both reigning Crystal Globe winners ) is likewise lining up for the 500 metres , 1,000 metres , 1,500 metres and relays . <p> Canadian speedskater William Dandjinou poses with a sculpture of a moose inside the Olympic Village in Milan on Tuesday . <p> Antonio Calanni/AP Toronto Star <p> In long track speedskating , the trio of Isabelle Weidemann , Ivanie Blondin and Val ? rie Maltais are looking to defend their Beijing title in the women 's team pursuit . Weidemann also won silver in the women 's 5,000 metres and bronze in the 3,000 metres four years ago , while Blondin added a silver in the women 's mass start . <p> The international cast of splendid athletes provides an abundance of riches on ice and snow . Among the most compelling : Unretired American skier Lindsey Vonn , aiming to become the oldest alpine medallist despite rupturing the ACL in her left knee in last week 's crash at the World Cup ; Marco ( the Swissblade ) Odermatt , arguably the best skier over the past four years , winner of four consecutive World Cup titles and three world championship gold medals ; American quad god figure skater Ilia Malinin . <p> Eileen Gu of China in action during the final run of the freeski slopestyle World Cup in Switzerland in January . <p> AP Toronto Star <p> More marquee athletes : Arianna Fontana , already Italy 's most dedicated Winter Olympian , keen on making it at least an even dozen in short-track ; Germany 's Francesco Friedrich chasing a sixth gold in bobsleigh ; China 's Eileen Gu , who became the first freestyle skier ever to win three medals at a singles Games in Beijing ; France 's Quentin Fillon Maillet , five biathlon medals in Beijing ; Japanese ski jumper Kobayashi Ryoyu . <p> And that 's just for starters . <p> Open your arms wide and let the Games begin . <p> Read more <p> Updated 4 hrs ago <h> It 's not just the athletes who are dreaming of gold . The Canadian Olympic Committee wants to host the Games again <p> Vancouver , home to Sidney Crosby 's goal in 2010 , was a candidate to host the Olympics again in 2030 , until the politics of the province changed . <p> Chris O'Meara/The Associated Press Toronto Star <p> MILAN -- Every Olympics is a time for hope , and the Canadian Olympic Committee stands at the front of the line . As Milan-Cortina begins , the COC is excited about our athletes , and about Canada 's chances , and pushing for a federal funding increase , and none of those are new . The COC also wants to host another Olympics , when possible , despite some recent false starts . A national Olympic federation can dream . <p> " The importance of hosting the Olympic Games in Canada is not lost on us , " said COC CEO and secretary general David Shoemaker , one day before the opening ceremony . " It 's something that we very much want to do . " <p> Canada has n't hosted a Games since Vancouver 2010 , after false starts with would-be bids for Calgary 2026 and Vancouver 2030 . Calgary would have renewed its creaking Olympic facilities , but was defeated by a referendum ; the COC had all but guaranteed Vancouver would host the 2030 Games , and then David Eby became the premier of B.C. and he could n't have pulled the plug harder if he tried . <p> Right now , the Swiss have the inside track on 2038 , but the COC is signalling it is eager to step forward if the Swiss fall through . Since Eby is still in charge in B.C. , it likely would n't be Vancouver . The Alberta government has been interested , though . And Shoemaker went further . Quebec City 's Olympic dreams have always been frustrated by the fact that their biggest mountain , Le Massif , is not nearly massif enough . <p> But Milan-Cortina is fuelling those dreams . The Italians have spread these Games all over the country ; it 's being called a dispersed Olympics , in a way no recent Games has attempted . It 's a reaction to the exhaustion of cities and countries who were willing to build every venue , and then watch them rot . <p> " ( Quebec ) always said that they do n't have a mountain , ( but ) this new model here in Milano Cortina ... we 're going to observe how dispersed games can work , " Shoemaker said . " We 're also thinking about how that could work in Canada to our advantage , including , you know , using some facilities in Western Canada . And , dare I say it , even Lake Placid . <p> " This new model ... I think puts the Summer Games into play for Canada that there 's an opportunity , let 's say , for communities from Quebec City all the way to Hamilton to be involved in a bid for the Summer Games that would probably have Montreal and Toronto as the leading edges ... That would be a real dream for me , but that 's a dream only , at this point . " <p> Indeed , that 's where everyone needs to pump the brakes . For Alberta to host an Olympics , the province would have to remain a part of Canada , and ideally the province 's separatist movement is crushed to allow for the discussion . But co-hosting an international event with the United States ... well , let 's just say the 2026 World Cup , and most coverage of current events , should show how bad an idea that is . And a dispersed Eastern Canada Summer Games ? It may be a bridge too far . <p> Still , at least the COC is thinking big , in more than one way . Canada has good reason for optimism in Milan : Canada has won between 24 and 29 medals at every Winter Games since Turin in 2006 , and projections put us back in that range here . <p> But the COC is also warning this could be a precipice , not a renewal . COC officials say the core of this team is still made up of athletes who were first identified in the 2014 NextGen talent identification program , and that a thinning Canadian athlete pool is coming . They point to federal funding that has been frozen since 2005 , which has caused sports federations to sacrifice grassroots development . And the reckoning may be coming . <p> " The reason is that with a lack of increase in federal government funding for national sports organizations in 20 years ... national sports organizations have had to make tough decisions , and those tough decisions are showing up in a few different places , " Shoemaker said . <p> COC chief sport officer Eric Myles also mentioned the expense of sports in Canada , and noted skicross -- a strong sport for Canada -- would have cost an athlete about $10,000 for a full-year camp in 2014 and is about $30,000 now , and that 's being reflected across different sports as funding is frozen and professionalization eats up the youth sport landscape . <p> " Membership that needs to be paid to be on the national team , we do n't see this in the other top competitor or top country that we compete against , " Myles said . <p> The COC recently lined up as many sponsors and partners as it could to create a $500-million goal for private fundraising and funding over the next decade , which Shoemaker says they can deliver . <p> An Olympics ? That will be a harder go . Still , in this tumultuous world , Canada is optimistic . Which , sadly , appears to be the sprawling and chopped-up fate of future Winter Games , starting with the generic " French Alps " hosting in 2030 . <p> Climate change is the primary culprit , rapidly shrinking the number of reliable hosts for the winter version of the quadrennial spectacle . A study published last month , building on recent research from the University of Waterloo , suggests that only about half of a possible 93 locations could reliably host the Winter Games , at least in February , by mid-century , if global warning continues its upwards trajectory . That research indicates snow-making would become a critical issue not far down the road -- and has been already , since at least Vancouver in 2010 . As I recall , Nagano in 1998 was a sloshy mess too . <p> Making the snow , rather than counting on what falls from the sky , has been used to some extent at every Winter Games since Lake Placid in 1980 , but Beijing was the first to rely on it almost entirely in 2022 . Without the manufactured version , the aforementioned research submits that only seven cities could reliably host the Games right now . <p> For these Games , organizers planned to make about 2.4 million cubic metres of snow .
